 SCCH-14 3 MVC..2235/2022  :JUDGMENT:
Petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 claiming Compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the death of Jagadeesh J.G. S/o Late Goligowda in the Motor Vehicle accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That, on 07032022 at about 1.00 p.m., Jagadeesh J.G was waiting to cross the road on NH48, TumkurBangalore road, near Yedehalli, Sompura Hobli,
Nelamangala Taluk, Bangalore Rural District.
At that time, the driver of Tata Intra goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA02AH6707 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Jagadeesh and caused the accident.
Due to the impact, Jagadeesh J.G sustained severe injuries all over the body.

Immediately the Jagadeesh was shifted to We Care hospital, Government hospital,
Dabaspet and Nelamangala Government hospital for treatment after few hours he died in the hospital.

sentences.text: Later postmortem examination was conducted at the same hospital and the body was handed over to the petitioners.

sentences.text: Jagadeesh J.G was aged 45 years as on the date of accident and was working as driver and earning sum of Rs.25,000/p.m.
The respondent No.1 is owner and respondent No.2 is insurer of Tata Intra goods vehicle.
As such, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The respondent No.3 is mother of the deceased/mother in law of petitioner No.1 and grand mother of petitioner No.2.
Hence, this petition.
3. Notice of this petition was duly served upon all the respondents.
However, the respondent No.1 and 2 made appearance through their respective learned advocates.
Respondent No.3 remained absent and placed exparte.
Though the respondent No.1 appeared did not choose to contest the petition.
Respondent No.2 contested the petition by filing statement of objection.

4. In the objections, the respondent No.2 denies the entire averments made in the petition, age,
avocation of the deceased.
It has denied the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Tata Intra goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA02AH6707 and its validity as on the date of accident.
However, its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

It is contended that the first respondent has violated the terms and conditions of the policy and has entrusted the offending vehicle in question to drive the same by a person who do not hold valid and effective driving licence,
FC and permit.
Further it has contended that accident occurred due to the negligence of deceased himself.
It is also contended that, the compensation claimed is exhorbitant.
With all these contentions it is prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. Based on the pleadings of the parties, materials placed on record this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioners prove that Jagadeesh J.G S/o Late Goligowda was died in the Road Traffic Accident which occurred on 0703 2022 at about 1.00 p.m. on NH48, Tumkur Bangalorae road, near Yedihalli, Sompura Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bangalore Rural District, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Tata Intra goods vehicle bearing No.KA 02AH6707 by its driver?
2. Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Jagadish.J.G?
3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?

4. What Order or Award?
6. In order to prove the case, the Petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW.1 and got marked documents Ex.P1 to Ex.P25 and closed their side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence.

sentences.text: Heard arguments of both sides.
Perused the pleadings, evidence and the materials placed on record.

My findings on the above issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No. 3 : Partly in the Affirmative.
 Issue No. 4 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS  8. Issue No.1: It is the case of the Petitioners that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Tata Intra goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA02AH6707 and in the said accident, Jagadeesh J.G had succumbed to the injuries.
9.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Tata Intra goods vehicle.

10. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as P.W.1 and she has filed her chief affidavit in lieu of chief examination and reiterated the petition averments.
11. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, PW.1 has relied on Ex.P1 to Ex.P12.

Ex.P1 and 2 are the True copies of FIR and complaint which shows that the Nelamangala Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of Tata Intra goods vehicle bearing No.KA02AH6707 for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337 of IPC.
Ex.P3 is the true copy of requisition submitted to the jurisdictional court.
Ex . P.4
is true copy of Outpatient slip.
Ex.P.5 is the true copy of PM Report which shows that the cause of death is due to massive internal haemorrhage and haemothorax secondary to chest injury.
Ex.P.6 is the true copy of Inquest panchanama.
Ex.P.7 is the true copy of Spot Panchanama along with spot sketch which shows that the concerned police have drawn Mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P.8 is the true copy of vehicle seizure panachanama which justify the fact of seizure of offending vehicle.
Ex.P.9 is the true copy of notice issued u/s 133 of IMV Act.

Ex.P.10 is the true copy of reply given in respect of Ex. P.9 notice which clarifies the fact as on the date of accident, the driver of offending vehicle possessed valid and effective driving licence to drive the same.
This document would also justify the fact of validity of policy as on the date of accident.
Ex.P.11 is the true copy of IMV Report which shows that accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the said motor vehicle.
Ex . P.12

is the true copy of the Chargesheet which shows that the I.O of Nelamangala Traffic Police Station has submitted Chargesheet against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 304(A) of IPC.
12.
Ex .P.13 and 14 are the notarized copies of Aadhar cards of Petitioner No.1 and 2.
Ex. P.15 is the notarized voter ID card of the deceased.

Ex. P.16 is the notarized copy of the PAN card of the Sharada vs M/S Rathore Marketing on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153225207/
4 deceased.
Ex. P.17
and 18
are the notarized copy of SSLC and PU marks card of petitioner No.2.
Ex.P.19 is the wedding invitation card of the petitioner No.1 and the deceased.

Ex.P.20 to 24 are the photographs and Ex.P.25 is CD.
13.
PW1 is subjected for cross examination by the learned counsel for Respondent No.2.

But,
nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the version of the Petitioners.
14. In order to rebut the evidence of petitioners, respondent has not adduced any rebuttal evidence.
15. Moreover, the charge sheet is the material document, which is not challenged by the driver of the offending vehicle.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence adduced by the Petitioner and the documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the Petitioner has proved that the said accident has occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Tata Intra goods vehicle bearing No.KA02AH6707 and in the said accident and the Jagadish had sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the "Affirmative".

Issue No. 2 and 3:
16.
Both these issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid the repetition of the facts.
17. It is stated in the Petition that the Petitioner No.1 is wife, petitioner No.2 is daughter and respondent No.3 is mother of the deceased Jagadeesh J.G.
In order to prove this fact, PW.1 has produced Ex.P13 to 16 i.e., Aadhar Card of petitioners and the Aadhar card of the deceased Jagadeesh J.G.
The document Ex. P.13, 14, 16, 17 to 19 justifies the fact that the petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased and the petitioner No.2 is the daughter of the deceased and the petitioner No.1.
The photographs mentioned above establishes the factum of performance of marriage of petitioner No.1 with the deceased which also corroborates the document Ex. P.19.
Apart from that, the police records also mentions regarding the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
Upon going through the said documents it clearly shows that the Petitioner No.1 and 2 and respondent No.3 are the legal heirs of the deceased Jagadeesh J.G.

Therefore, the Petitioners are considered as the dependents of the deceased Jagadeesh J.G.
18.
In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 45 years and his avocation is shown as driver and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/ per month.
In this regard, petitioner has not produced any supportive documents to show that avocation and income of the deceased.

Therefore, in the absence of any income proof, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, since the accident has been occurred in the year 2022, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e. 15,500/ p.m. for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
19. Further, the Petitioners have stated the age of the deceased Jagadeesh J.G as 45 years at the time of the accident.
As per the document Ex. P.15, I.e., notarized copy of Voter ID of the deceased Jagadeesh J.G as on 01.01.2004 his age was shown as 25 years.

If the same is considered along with Sharada vs M/S Rathore Marketing on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153225207/
5 the documents Ex. P.5 and 6, it appears that Ex. P.5 and 6 reflects that the deceased was of the age 50 years when the procedure of inquest panchanama and post mortem were conducted.
In the absence of furnishing of any supportive document by the petitioners to show that the deceased was of 45 years old, there appears no reasons to disbelieve the age mentioned in Ex. P.5 and 6.
Accordingly, the age of the deceased Jagadeesh J.G is considered as 50 years for the purpose of Assessment of compensation.
20. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
21.

The deceased has left behind him, his mother i.e., respondent No.3, his wife and daughter I.e,
petitioner No.1 and 2..
Hence, the respondent No.3 and the Petitioners No.1 and 2 are considered as the dependents of the deceased.

At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that : "Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/ and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/".

entities.text: Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In Civil Appeal No.24102412 of 2023 between Shriram General Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Bhagat Singh Ravat and others with SLP(C)
Nos.11851186/2021, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that "Having said so, learned counsel for the respondent points out that this amount so determined by us is liable to be enhanced by a percentage of 10 per cent every 3 years as opined in para 61 (viii) of the judgement in Pranay Sethi's case (supra) which reads as under: 61(viii) Reasonable figures on conventional heads,
namely, loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/ Rs.40,000/
and Rs.15,000/ respectively.

Shriram General Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Bhagat Singh Ravat and others with SLP(C)
Nos.11851186/2021
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced @ 10% in every three years."

As this Court has already observed that the Petitioner No.1 is wife of the deceased, petitioner No.2 is daughter and respondent No.3 is the mother of the deceased Jagadeesh J.G, the Petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rupees 44,000/ towards loss of consortium and Rupees 16,500/ towards loss of estate and Rupees 16,500/ towards funeral expenses.

IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION,
22.
Petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased and she lost her husband's love and care.
Petitioner No.2 is the daughter of the deceased and she lost her father's love and care and respondent No.3 is mother of the deceased and she lost her son's love and care.
Bearing in mind the relationship of the Petitioners and respondent No.3 with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:

sentences.text: The Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.10,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF DEPENDANCY:

24. It is pertinent to note here that as per the detailed discussion as made supra, the income of the deceased was notionally fixed at Rs.15,500/ p.m.
25.

At this juncture, I would like to go through the decision reported in :
1) 2018 ACJ 740, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India At New Delhi in between Manuswamy and others V/s.
Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Trans. Corpn. Ltd, wherein it is held as under:
"Quantum fatal accident Principle of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged :
21, contract worker in a company - High Court did not consider future prospects while computing compensation - Whether claimants are entitled to compensation after addition of 40 per cent of income of the deceased towards future prospects "

entities.text: Supreme Court of India At New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

entities.text:
Manuswamy and others V/s.
Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Trans. Corpn. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Held :  yes.
2) 2018 ACJ 5, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, at New Delhi in between Hem Raj Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., and others wherein it is held as under :
"Quantum Fatal accident - Principles of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged 40 Upholding objections of insurance company that principle of addition on account of future prospects is not applicable where income of the deceased is determined by guesswork, High Court disallowed the addition of 50 per cent made by the Tribunal for future prospects while computing compensation -

entities.text: Hem Raj Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Whether addition on account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guesswork in absence of proof of income Held: Yes: there cannot be distinction where there is evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guesswork:
executing Court directed to respondent compute entitlement of claimants by adding 40 per cent of income for future prospect and make corresponding deduction towards personal expenses".
The decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that: "In case self employed or person on fixed salary the addition should be 10% when the age is between 50 to 60 years".

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this Petition, the deceased was aged 50 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 10% of the income has to be added.
So, 10% of Rs.15,500/ comes to Rs.1,550/.
Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.17,050/ p.m. (Rs.15,500/ + Rs.1,550/).

sentences.text: Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 11.

entities.text: (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that where the number of dependent of family members is 2 to 3, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

26. After deducting 1/3rd towards his personal expenses in Rs.19,375/ it comes to Rs.11,367/
(Rs.17,050/  5,683/) and multiplier applied is 11 which comes to Rs.15,00,444/ (11,367 x 12 x 11).
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.15,00,444/ which is rounded off to Rs.15,00,500/ towards loss of dependency.

27. TOTAL QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED:
1. Loss of consortium Rs. 44,000/
2. Loss of Love and Affection Rs. 50,000/
3. Loss of Estate Rs. 16,500/
4. Funeral Expenses Rs. 16,500/
5. Expenses of transportation Rs. 10,000/ of dead body 6. Loss of Dependency Rs. 15,00,500/ Total Rs.16,37,500/

Thus, totally the Petitioners and the respondent No.3 ares awarded compensation of Rs.16,37,500/
with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.
28. Regarding Liability : As already discussed in the Issue No.1, in this case the driver of the offending Tata Intra goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA02AH6707 was charge sheeted.

Further,
there is no dispute about the validity of the Insurance Policy of the offending vehicle as on the date of accident.
Moreover, there is no proof of allegation of the fact that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess the valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.

Therefore,
Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners and to the respondent No.3.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the "Affirmative" and Issue No. 3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
29. Issue No.4 :

From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioners and the respondent No.3 are entitled for compensation of Rs.16,37,500/ along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.
In the result, I proceed to pass the following :

ORDER The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

Whether the Petitioners prove that Jagadeesh J.G S/o Late Goligowda was died in the Road Traffic Accident which occurred on 0703 2022 at about 1.00 p.m. on NH48, Tumkur Bangalorae road, near Yedihalli, Sompura Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bangalore Rural District, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Tata Intra goods vehicle bearing No.KA 02AH6707 by its driver?
2. Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Jagadish.J.G?
3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
My findings on the above issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No. 3 : Partly in the Affirmative.
 Issue No. 4 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS  8. Issue No.1: It is the case of the Petitioners that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Tata Intra goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA02AH6707 and in the said accident, Jagadeesh J.G had succumbed to the injuries.
9.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
15. Moreover, the charge sheet is the material document, which is not challenged by the driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence adduced by the Petitioner and the documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the Petitioner has proved that the said accident has occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Tata Intra goods vehicle bearing No.KA02AH6707 and in the said accident and the Jagadish had sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
Therefore, in the absence of any income proof, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, since the accident has been occurred in the year 2022, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e. 15,500/ p.m. for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
19. Further, the Petitioners have stated the age of the deceased Jagadeesh J.G as 45 years at the time of the accident.
In the absence of furnishing of any supportive document by the petitioners to show that the deceased was of 45 years old, there appears no reasons to disbelieve the age mentioned in Ex. P.5 and 6.
Accordingly, the age of the deceased Jagadeesh J.G is considered as 50 years for the purpose of Assessment of compensation.
The deceased has left behind him, his mother i.e., respondent No.3, his wife and daughter I.e,
petitioner No.1 and 2..
Hence, the respondent No.3 and the Petitioners No.1 and 2 are considered as the dependents of the deceased.
In Civil Appeal No.24102412 of 2023 between Shriram General Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Bhagat Singh Ravat and others with SLP(C)
Nos.11851186/2021, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that "Having said so, learned counsel for the respondent points out that this amount so determined by us is liable to be enhanced by a percentage of 10 per cent every 3 years as opined in para 61 (viii) of the judgement in Pranay Sethi's case (supra) which reads as under: 61(viii) Reasonable figures on conventional heads,
namely, loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/ Rs.40,000/
and Rs.15,000/ respectively.
Petitioner No.2 is the daughter of the deceased and she lost her father's love and care and respondent No.3 is mother of the deceased and she lost her son's love and care.
Sharada vs M/S Rathore Marketing on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153225207/
7
Further,
there is no dispute about the validity of the Insurance Policy of the offending vehicle as on the date of accident.
Moreover, there is no proof of allegation of the fact that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess the valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Therefore,
Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners and to the respondent No.3.

Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.15,00,444/ which is rounded off to Rs.15,00,500/ towards loss of dependency.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the "Affirmative" and Issue No. 3 "Partly in the Affirmative".

From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioners and the respondent No.3 are entitled for compensation of Rs.16,37,500/ along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.
In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
